newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenyan air cargo perishables market to expand.
newsitem.headline: Kenyan air cargo perishables market to expand.

text.p: Kenya's air cargo market has expanded considerably over the past few years and freight forwarders expect this trend to continue, a Dutch forwarder here said on Wednesday.

Johan van de Put, managing director of his own "Fresh Cargo Handling BV" company, said the business of flying out fresh produce from Kenya's horticulture industry had grown by more than 20 percent in the past year.

The Dutch company now exports around of 500 tonnes of air cargo a week from East and Southern Africa, he said. It has been handling air cargo exports of fruits, vegetables and flowers for more than 20 years.

"I think there will be a continued growing market here for us of up to 800 tonnes a week," said van de Put, adding that "there are almost no other exports" than fresh produce which are shipped out of the East African region by air.

"We have a total of 11 to 12 flights a week from Nairobi to Europe, of which 95 percent of the cargo is fresh produce. Larger planes -- Boeing 747s and McDonnell Douglas MD-11 -- are being used, mainly from Kenya, but also now from Zimbabwe."

"For sure there is an export increase. This year, for the 1996/97 season of fresh produce (ending mid-August), there has been an rise of 20 percent in the volume of freight we have handled, due to both arrival of new clients and clients who have increased their volume," van de Put told Reuters.
Van de Put, citing commercial reasons for declining to give exact figures, said the production of fresh produce in the region was likely to continue to increase over the years to come.
"The total production of fresh produce is increasing and since such cargo always will be transported by air, the air cargo market will automatically continue to increase," he added.
